title: AI Agents and Infrastructure Face Political Scrutiny Post-Midterms
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- AI agents gain traction as a business model despite skepticism over their utility in real estate.
- Midterm election results signal a potential shift toward stricter AI regulation and data center opposition.
- Anthropic continues to refine Claude's safety and code review processes.
- OpenAI is launching new infrastructure initiatives to manage data center power usage.

Interest in AI agents is rising as developers explore new business models, though real-world application remains a point of debate. While some see agents as a service, industry leaders like Zillow's CEO remain skeptical about their role in complex tasks like home buying. Simultaneously, the field of software engineering is evolving, with new tools like Meta's acquisition of Conductor aiming to deploy agent teams to assist developers, reinforcing the view that AI will transform rather than replace developer roles.

Political headwinds are intensifying following the midterm elections, with rising concerns over AI regulation and infrastructure. Voters have shown increased resistance to data center expansion, prompting tech companies to seek new strategies. OpenAI is responding by launching programs like 'Grid Protectors' to address power concerns, while Google faces backlash for its policy regarding search access in schools that restrict AI. As the industry navigates this new era of scrutiny, Anthropic is focusing on internal safety, reporting that Claude is significantly more effective at identifying unsafe actions than human reviewers.
